newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S'pore oil products surge on U.S. missile strike.
newsitem.headline: S'pore oil products surge on U.S. missile strike.

text.p: Singapore oil products surged on news of a U.S. missile attack on Iraq earlier Tuesday but eased later in the day on profit-taking, traders said.

October gas oil swaps rose to a five-year high to trade at $28.10, up a hefty $1.50 from the previous close. Prices eased later on profit taking and lower crude values to close around $27.70. The market was dominated by swaps business with physical players largely sidelined due to the volatile trading.
They emerged later and a Singapore-based trader sold 220,000 barrels lifting end Sept/early October at $27.60 and 150,000 barrels lifting end September at $27.65, both fob Singapore.

Refiners were optimistic that physical prices would rise in tandem with the swaps numbers as supplies tightened in the absence of arbitrage cargoes. Traders were not expected to plan any gas oil exports from the west to Asia as prices in Asia are lagging those in the west, one refiner said.
Jet fuel prices soared to a pre-winter high with September swaps bids at $31 against no firm offers, brokers said. A bid for 100,000 barrels lifting end-September at $29.90 failed to secure a sale.
Naphtha rose to its highest post-Gulf War level at $21.50 but was unlikley to improve the $31.50 reached in January 1991.
Buyers were jittery and Taiwan even considered cancelling an October buy tender for 30,000 tonnes of heavy naphtha.
But mounting tensions saw prices on a sustained upward trend and Taiwan decided to purchase the cargo at around $200 per tonne, an official said.
A major was heard to buy 50,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded gasoline at $23.50 for September 21-25 and still bidding at the same level, higher than Monday's $23.00/$23.45.
Fuel oil rose by $6 to $114.50 per tonne but traders were cautious watching further developments on U.S./Iraq tension.
